newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik president wounded in assassination bid.
newsitem.headline: Tajik president wounded in assassination bid.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov was wounded in an assassination attempt on Wednesday and taken to hospital where he was in a stable condition, his spokesman said.

"At 10.30 am (0530 GMT), in the town of Khudjand in the Leninabad region, a terrorist act was carried out against President Imomali Rakhmonov," Zafar Saidov, the president's press secretary, told Reuters in the capital Dushanbe.
He said Rakhmonov was on his way from a function marking the 65th anniversary of the northern town's university to a nearby theatre when a grenade was thrown at his feet as he got out of a car.
At least two other officials were wounded but there were no reports of any deaths.
"The president is in a hospital in Khudjand and his condition is stable," Saidov said.

Saidov said 21-year-old Firdavs Dustboboyev, who he said organised an anti-government protest in the town in May last year, was responsible for the attack and was apprehended by security officials almost immediately afterwards.
"This was a terrorist act of a purely political nature," Saidov said.

Tajikistan, a former Soviet republic, is still reeling from a four-year civil war in which tens of thousands of people were killed. Armed groups still roam the mountain state which borders Afghanistan and China.
